notes.note: The import meter at Fenside Arable shows -1,284.0 kWh for 14 Sep 2026: the register read fell from 666,757.8 to 665,473.8 kWh. A negative advance cannot be real consumption, so the day is held out of the validated totals and September will be one day short for this site until it is resolved.
notes.likely_cause: Most likely a meter exchange or register reset on 14 Sep that has not been recorded, or an incorrect read keyed for that day. The readings either side look normal, which points to a one-off step in the register rather than a faulty meter.
notes.suggested_action: Check with the supplier or meter operator for a meter exchange on or around 14 Sep 2026 and obtain the closing and opening reads before the day is re-included.

notes.note: There are no readings for the import meter at Westcombe Orchards for 7 days, 12-18 Sep 2026. The register advanced 5,542.9 kWh between the reads either side of the gap, so the consumption is not lost, but September is incomplete for supplier bill validation.
notes.likely_cause: Most likely a communications outage on the meter or a failed data collection for those days.
notes.suggested_action: Request the missing daily reads from the data collector; if they cannot be recovered, agree whether to apportion the 5,542.9 kWh register advance across the seven days.

notes.note: All 92 readings for 01 Aug-31 Oct 2026 in the electricity import export use meter serial E17UP04521, which is not in the site register. The register's E17UP04512 (Oakleigh Equestrian Centre, Melton Mowbray) has no readings at all, and the two serials differ only by the last two digits being swapped.
notes.likely_cause: Most likely a transposition error in the serial, either in the supplier export or in the site register.
notes.suggested_action: Confirm the serial on the meter or a recent bill for Oakleigh Equestrian Centre, then correct the export mapping or the register; the readings stay out of the totals until then.

notes.note: The 05 Oct 2026 reading for the import meter at Redhill Pig Unit appears twice in the export, as 735.5 kWh and 1,471.0 kWh, with the same register read of 288,603.3 kWh. The second figure is exactly double the first, so keeping both would overstate October consumption.
notes.likely_cause: Most likely the day was loaded twice and the second row double-counted. Which value is right should be confirmed, not assumed.
notes.suggested_action: Ask the data provider which value is correct for 05 Oct and remove the other row from the source data before the October supplier report.

notes.note: Penrose Farm's 50 kWp array is recorded as generating 2,450.0 kWh on 22 Aug 2026, more than six times the 400.0 kWh a system of that size could produce in a day. The generation meter register advanced by 245.0 kWh that day, in line with the 130.5-210.4 kWh recorded on neighbouring days.
notes.likely_cause: Most likely a decimal-place slip in the export (245.0 recorded as 2,450.0); the register reads themselves look consistent.
notes.suggested_action: Confirm the 245.0 kWh figure against the register reads and correct the export before the FIT generation readings are sent.

notes.note: The solar PV generation meter at Bryn Mawr Farm recorded zero for 9 consecutive days, 08-16 Aug 2026, in the middle of summer. Generation either side averaged about 538.6 kWh a day, so roughly 4,847 kWh may not have been generated or recorded, which could affect this quarter's FIT readings and payments.
notes.likely_cause: Possibly an inverter trip or an isolator left off, in which case the energy was genuinely not generated; a fault in the generation meter is less likely but possible.
notes.suggested_action: Contact the site to check the inverter logs for 08-16 Aug and confirm whether the system was generating; record the outcome before the FIT readings are submitted.
